intent: Keep the race 8 platform (five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03, y = 0.06, body_length 0.12 m, 0.8 kg, 3 cm wheels) and change one variable: wheel_track 0.12 m to 0.10 m, to raise yaw response for slalom. I expect slalom line loss to fall below 1 and slalom finishes to rise above 2/20, with max_error below 0.06. I expect oval finishes to hold at 18 or more of 20 and oval steering_oscillation to stay below 0.3. The Integrator should rescale kp to about 2.7 for the narrower track. I am not changing mass or sensors in the same step. If the result is worse, I will revert wheel_track to 0.12 m.
learning: Race 8 showed that yaw inertia (body_length) was part of the slalom limit: slalom finishes rose from 0 to 2/20 and line loss fell from 1.2 to 1.0, with oval and s-bend held. Yaw inertia alone does not clear slalom. Next race: if slalom line loss drops below 1 with wheel_track 0.10 and kp about 2.7, yaw authority is the limit and I will keep it. If slalom line loss is unchanged or worse, the next test is controller response (kd) rather than geometry.
rationale: Race 8 (body_length 0.12 m, otherwise race 7) is the best result so far at 742.12, up from 636.91. Oval stayed at 20/20 with steering_oscillation 0.221, down from 0.230. S-bend stayed strong at 20/20, and slalom rose from 0/20 to 2/20 finishes. Slalom line loss fell from 1.2 to 1.0 and its max_error stayed at the 0.06 limit. The Integrator's rule was to keep body_length 0.12 if slalom line loss fell below 1. It is exactly 1.0, so the rule is not cleanly met. The improvement is real, though: slalom finishes appeared, the score rose, and oval oscillation improved. I am keeping body_length 0.12 m. The Integrator's fallback is the next step: the yaw response is still limiting slalom. Here I follow the Integrator's wheel_track 0.10 request, changing one geometry variable only. Mass stays at 0.8 kg, as the Integrator asked. Lowering wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m raises yaw gain per unit wheel-speed difference by about 1.2 times, so the Integrator should rescale kp from 3.2 to about 2.7 to hold steering authority. Sensors, wheel radius, body width and mass are unchanged, so the wheel_track effect can be read against race 8. Expected result: slalom line loss falls below 1 and slalom finishes rise, while oval and s-bend hold near race 8 levels. If oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.35 or slalom line loss rises, I will revert wheel_track to 0.12 m and hold the race 8 platform for gain tuning.
